what_it_does: Safety-critical systems — car brakes, airbags, industrial controllers — must prove they will still work correctly even if a transistor on their chip quietly fails. The standard way to verify this is to run diagnostic test patterns during a dedicated test mode, but traditional test-generation tools (which scan every possible stuck fault) require special extra hardware and must halt normal operation, which is disruptive and costly for systems that run continuously in the field. This paper proposes using reinforcement learning (an AI technique where an agent learns by trial and error, earning rewards for good outcomes) to automatically generate a library of test programs — short sequences of ordinary chip instructions — that can be injected during idle moments without any extra hardware, without stopping the system, and while achieving high coverage of the faults that matter for functional safety. The learning agent explores the chip's own instruction set to discover patterns that exercise as many failure modes as possible.
